english_paragraphs: In July 1909, BASF envoys gathered round a squat machine on a bench in Fritz Haber's Karlsruhe laboratory. Behind its gleaming, bolted valves, nitrogen and hydrogen met at crushing pressure and furnace heat, and transparent beads of ammonia began to drip slowly. Haber had pried nourishment from the air.

BASF's Carl Bosch scaled the method up, and from 1913 a gigantic plant at Oppau mass-produced ammonia. Hailed for making bread from air, Haber won the coveted 1918 Nobel Prize. Ploughed into stony soils as fertiliser, ammonia wards off famine as no manure heap could, bringing abundance. By 2008 it was feeding nearly half of mankind.

Haber's ambition had a sinister side. Ammonia stocked Germany's arsenal with nitrates for munitions despite a British blockade, and Captain Haber marshalled chemical warfare. On 22 April 1915 at Ypres, troops vented about 168 tonnes of greenish, poisonous chlorine towards the Allied trenches, the first large-scale gas onslaught.

Haber's wife, Clara Immerwahr, Germany's first woman with a doctoral degree in chemistry, voiced objections to his work. On 2 May 1915, after festivities in his honour, she shot herself in the garden with his service pistol. The next day the widower left for the Eastern Front.

Prestige offered no sanctuary. Of Jewish origin, Haber left Germany an outcast after Hitler's regime seized power, dying in Basel in 1934. His institute's pesticide research had produced Zyklon. A later variant, Zyklon B, was used in Nazi death camps, where relatives of his died.
About half the nitrogen in our proteins and DNA has passed through a Haber-Bosch factory, so each of us carries a little of Haber's chemistry.
chinese_paragraphs: 1909年7月，BASF公司的代表围在弗里茨·哈伯位于卡尔斯鲁厄的实验室工作台旁，看着一台矮壮的机器。在闪亮、用螺栓紧固的阀门后，氮与氢在极高压力和熔炉般的高温下反应，透明的氨液滴开始缓缓滴落。哈伯从空气中撬出了养分。
BASF的卡尔·博施将这一方法扩大到工业规模。1913年起，奥保的一座大型工厂开始批量生产氨。哈伯因“从空气中造面包”而广受赞誉，获得了令人向往的1918年诺贝尔奖。氨作为化肥被施入多石的土壤，以粪肥远不能及的能力抵御饥荒，带来丰收。到2008年，它已养活近半数人类。
哈伯的雄心也有阴暗的一面。尽管英国实施封锁，氨仍为德国军火库提供制造弹药所需的硝酸盐；而哈伯上尉则组织化学战。1915年4月22日，在伊普尔，德军向协约国战壕排放了约168吨黄绿色的有毒氯气，发动了首次大规模毒气攻击。
哈伯的妻子克拉拉·伊梅瓦尔是德国首位获得化学博士学位的女性，她曾反对他的工作。1915年5月2日，在为哈伯举行的庆祝活动之后，她在花园中用他的军用手枪自杀。次日，这位刚刚丧妻的人便前往东线。
声望并未给哈伯提供庇护。身为犹太裔，他在希特勒政权掌权后受到排斥，离开德国，1934年死于巴塞尔。他所在研究所的杀虫剂研究曾催生齐克隆；后来的变体齐克隆B被用于纳粹死亡营，他的一些亲属也死在这些营中。
我们体内蛋白质和DNA所含的氮，约有一半曾经过哈伯—博施工厂。因此，每个人的身体里都带着一点哈伯化学的痕迹。

illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

Article 16, The Bread Made from Air. Show the pivotal 1909 ammonia synthesis demonstration in Fritz Haber's Karlsruhe laboratory. The central object is a compact, stout early-twentieth-century high-pressure steel apparatus on a wooden laboratory bench, with heavy bolted valves, realistically connected metal pipes, a small heated reaction section and a closed clear collection receiver in which a few transparent liquid beads are visible. Two attentive scientists in restrained 1909 civilian laboratory dress observe the apparatus, secondary to the mechanism, with natural hands and faces. A few wheat ears rest unobtrusively beside the bench as a restrained editorial link to ammonia fertiliser and food, not bread magically materialising out of air. Ivory laboratory walls, sage shaded glass and metal, very restrained warm brass and wheat accents. Emphasise careful experimental work and the later food application without triumphalist hero worship. No open cloud of toxic gas, no weapons, no dead or injured figures, no Nazi emblems, no implication that Haber personally invented Zyklon B. No chemical formulas, labels, gauge numerals, text or fake equations. Keep the steel reaction apparatus plausible, not a fantasy glass chemistry toy.
approved_summary: 1909年哈伯用空气里的氮，在高温高压下与氢合成氨；博施将其放大，1913年实现工业量产。
氨制成化肥，提高粮食产量，到2008年已支撑近半人类；人体蛋白质和DNA中约一半的氮也经此工艺。
合成氨也供应弹药原料；哈伯1915年组织首次大规模毒气攻击，妻子反对其战争工作。
妻子后来自杀，他次日仍赴前线；虽获1918年诺奖，犹太裔的他后来仍遭纳粹排斥，1934年死于流亡中。
他研究所的杀虫剂齐克隆，后来衍生出齐克隆B；纳粹将其用于死亡营，他的一些亲属也死在营中。
